q: A plain Parquet folder and a Delta table hold exactly the same Parquet files. What makes the Delta table able to offer transactions and time travel?
o: A special Delta file format instead of Parquet
The `_delta_log` transaction log next to the files
A lock server that runs on the cluster
Copies of every file kept in a hidden folder
e: The data files are ordinary Parquet. The transaction log records which files belong to each version, and every feature in this module is built on it.

q: You append a DataFrame with a new column `channel` to a Delta table, using `.option("mergeSchema", "true")`. What happens to the rows that were already in the table?
o: They are rewritten with an empty `channel` value
The append fails because the schemas differ
Nothing is rewritten: old rows read `NULL` for `channel`
They are deleted and replaced
e: Schema evolution only changes the schema in the log. Existing files are not touched; their rows return NULL for the new column.

q: A MERGE fails with an error about multiple source rows matching the same target row. What is the right fix?
o: Deduplicate the source so each key appears once
Switch the table to Serializable isolation
Run OPTIMIZE on the target first
Add `mergeSchema` to the MERGE
e: MERGE refuses to guess which source row should win. Keep one row per key in the source, for example the latest one.

q: You run `RESTORE TABLE orders TO VERSION AS OF 5` while the table is at version 9. What does the history look like afterwards?
o: Versions 6 to 9 are deleted from the history
The table is back at version 5 and the next write creates version 6
Version 5 is copied over version 9
A new version 10 that has the data of version 5; versions 6 to 9 stay in the history
e: RESTORE is a normal commit. It adds a new version that looks like the old one, so the undo itself is recorded and nothing in the history is rewritten.

q: A stream with `trigger(availableNow=True)` reads a Delta table and has already processed it once. 100 rows are appended to the source. What does the next run of the same stream, with the same checkpoint, read?
o: The whole table again
Only the 100 new rows
Nothing until the checkpoint is deleted
Only the rows that changed since the last OPTIMIZE
e: The checkpoint stores the last source version the stream processed, so the next run reads only the commits after it.
